issues.reason: The intransitive-subject test puts a 'non-volitional natural process / force — precipitation, fluids, gases' on Patient even when the verb is motion-like ('smoke rose', 'the tide receded'), so (Agent $b $w) for a wind blowing asserts the volitional-doer reading the rule denies it.

gaps_confirmed: An adjectivally-restricted bare-plural object ('unprepared lanterns') inside a rule CONSEQUENT has no stated route: a bare kind filler cannot carry the descriptive adjective, a consequent-minted group cannot carry the per-member distribution the adjective would need (rules do not nest), and universalizing the lantern into the premise — what this parse does — silently strengthens the claim to every unprepared lantern.
defect_summary: The compliant form replaces (Agent $b $w) in the premise with (Patient $b $w); the consequent's (Agent (sk_extinguish $b $l) $w) is correct as it stands, since a transitive subject stays Agent even when inanimate and non-volitional.
notes: The confirmed gap's improvisation is otherwise graceful — the nearest precedent, an adjectivally-restricted kind subject forcing the distributing-rule route with 'the restriction becomes a premise conjunct', is the same move applied to an object. The rest is doctrinal: whenever takes the rule form with no QuantifierPhrase, 'cold'/'unprepared' stay non-fusing descriptive atoms, 'off the sea' is Source with the sea asserted top-level so the sk_ constant in the premise is licensed, and 'at night' is the day-part Time symbol.
